segments.title: Chương 78: 0078【Ba người bạn】
segments.content:
"Holy shit, they caught Ma Jiajue!"

It was unclear who in the classroom shouted it, but in an instant, a dozen or so people crowded around to look at the newspaper.

"Where did they catch him?"

"Sanya."

"Didn't he kill people in Yunnan Province? He really fled to the ends of the earth."

"He'll definitely get the death penalty this time."

"Duh, he killed four classmates. How could he not get the death penalty?"

"..."

In the second semester of the third year of high school, we couldn't even watch *Legal Report* anymore, but several newspapers would appear in the classroom every day.

The newspapers were brought in by Gao Zhan, the politics teacher. The *People's Daily* and *Global Times* were there every day, for students to read more and learn about current events. Occasionally, he would also get a copy of the *West China Metropolis Daily*, which was purely for the students' amusement.

This issue of the *West China Metropolis Daily* dedicated an entire page to reporting on Ma Jiajue's capture and discussing students' psychological issues.

Among the general student population, Ma Jiajue had already become a running joke.

"Thank you, roommates, for the mercy of not killing me!"

"I'll hammer you to death!"

Chen Guiliang was in a daze from doing practice problems. When he heard the name "Ma Jiajue," he suddenly couldn't tell if he had been reborn or not.

Forget it, I'll just put my head down and sleep for a bit.

He felt that he had been getting a bit obsessive recently. In order to secure a spot at Peking University, he was studying too hard and had lost the detached mindset of a reincarnator.

Damn it, I didn't even work this hard in my third year of high school in my past life.

I have to make an adjustment.

After sleeping for half an hour, Chen Guiliang felt his mind was much clearer.

"You're awake?" his deskmate, Qin Shanshan, said.

Chen Guiliang yawned, "Not enough sleep yet."

Qin Shanshan said, "I really envy you. At least you have a clear goal. I'm just very lost, I don't know what I'm studying for."

Chen Guiliang thought: You'll know why you're studying next year when you repeat this grade.

This deskmate of his only made it into a third-tier university, didn't even bother filling out her application, and went straight to buy review materials.

Chen Guiliang took out his politics practice paper and continued to use his consistent review method—

For questions he was one hundred percent sure he could answer, he just scanned them and didn't bother wasting time writing them down.

If he encountered one he wasn't sure about, he would flip through the book to find the answer. He would then think about why he wasn't sure. If it involved multiple knowledge points, he would stop and read the book carefully to master all the related concepts.

If he knew the general direction of the answer but couldn't write out the complete details, it was usually a more difficult essay question. At this point, he had to pick up his pen, copy the answer from the book, and then spend time memorizing it.

By doing this, every time he finished a practice paper, he would master a few knowledge points he had missed.

Every half-month, he would read through the outline of the entire textbook, and then read the detailed outline of each unit more closely. Combined with his review over the past half-month, he gained a more systematic and comprehensive understanding of the entire textbook. He had completely mastered the book.

Of course, this method wasn't very useful for English, because Chen Guiliang didn't know too many words, was unfamiliar with too many phrase usages...

The evening self-study session ended.

Chen Guiliang decided not to stay up late tonight. Empty-handed, he went for a walk around campus.

To clear his head.

He walked over to Bian Guanyue and said with a smile, "I'll walk you to the bus stop."

"Okay," Bian Guanyue was particularly delighted, but her expression didn't change much, as there were still many classmates in the room.

"Ooh~~~~"

Several students in the first two rows near the middle heard their conversation and immediately started hooting and jeering.

Bian Guanyue finally couldn't maintain her composure, and her face flushed red all the way to her ears.

The two walked out of the classroom side by side. Bian Guanyue was so shy she lowered her head and didn't speak.

"Great Hero Chen!"

Ou Yafei from the neighboring class took the initiative to greet Chen Guiliang for the first time.

Chen Guiliang nodded in response, "Hello, Classmate Ou."

Ou Yafei said in surprise, "Great Hero Chen, you know who I am?"

"It's hard not to," Chen Guiliang said with a smile.

Ou Yafei then looked at Bian Guanyue and commented, "You two are a good match, talented and beautiful. See you!"

"See you."

Towards the white moonlight of his past life, Chen Guiliang now treated her with a calm heart, and he couldn't be bothered to pry into other people's private lives.

The abortion thing, maybe it was true, maybe it was false, but it had nothing to do with him.

"Great Hero Chen!"

Another student from the same grade greeted him.

Chen Guiliang smiled and waved, enjoying the treatment of a celebrity ahead of time.

Bian Guanyue said, "The whole school knows you now, especially the third-year students."

Chen Guiliang laughed heartily. "I've always been famous among the third-years. Last year, I went from classroom to classroom looking for their signatures. Even if they didn't know my name, they knew there was a psycho who got their computer lab fees back for them."

"You're very brave," Bian Guanyue said admiringly.

The two chatted idly all the way and soon arrived at the bus stop outside the school.

Chen Guiliang said, "After the first mock exam is over, I'm going to buy a cell phone and a repeater. Are you free?"

"Um... yes, I'm free." Bian Guanyue felt a sweetness in her heart.

The first mock exam was tomorrow.

The mock exam papers were created by the city's education bureau, and the quality was much better than the monthly tests.

At least, Chen Guiliang didn't find any more obvious flaws in the questions.

The Chinese exam was a breeze, especially the reading comprehension. Chen Guiliang's first consideration was the intent of the test creator, not the original author's intent. Once he figured out why a question was asked in a certain way, the answer he wrote would be more or less correct.

Math, Chen Guiliang did pretty well.

English, still suffering from an insufficient vocabulary.

Liberal Arts Comprehensive, Chen Guiliang had never let this slide. Even after he started working, he would still find books to read on his own. His reserve of knowledge in politics, history, and geography was extremely rich.

The points he had lost on the Liberal Arts Comprehensive in previous tests were mainly on theoretical essay questions and some less common high school knowledge points.

After the first mock exam, there was a one-day break.

The teachers had to hurry and grade the papers and report the scores to the city for a unified score estimation and mock admission cutoff line.

On this day off, the third-year students, who had been cooped up for too long, went wild everywhere in various ways.

Well, there were also some who slept the whole day!

Just as Chen Guiliang was about to leave the dormitory, he received a call from Tao Xue. "Big Nephew, I'm outside your dorm."

Aunt Tao had long been waiting for the third-years' day off...

When Bian Guanyue stood at the crossroads and saw Chen Guiliang get out of the car, she also saw Tao Xue behind him.

She instantly became a little displeased.

"Aunt Xue wanted to go shopping too," Chen Guiliang said helplessly.

"Hi!"

Tao Xue waved enthusiastically with a brilliant smile. "Senior Sister, we meet again."

"Hello."

Bian Guanyue offered a polite greeting, thinking: I'm going to get into a university in Beijing. By then, you'll still be a second-year in this county town. Let's see you be a tag-along then!

By then, you can hold the baby for me. One boy and two girls, first they went to find a place to eat.

Chen Guiliang and Tao Xue hadn't had a chance to eat breakfast yet, while Bian Guanyue had deliberately saved her appetite. She had eaten until she was stuffed when they bought the cat last semester.

The atmosphere at the dinner table was okay. Tao Xue chattered away.

Bian Guanyue was also considerate and didn't remain silent, chatting with Tao Xue from time to time.

After they finished breakfast, they strolled toward the commercial street in the new district. From a distance, a song could be heard: "The thirty-six stratagems of love, are just like a game, I want to control the remote myself..."

Tao Xue said, "This album is super popular. It was just released last week."

Actually, it had been released for over half a month, but things were half a beat slower in this small county town.

Bian Guanyue had been busy studying recently and hadn't paid much attention. "Sounds like Jolin Tsai's voice? I heard it on the school radio the other day."

"Yeah, it's Jolin Tsai's new album," Tao Xue said with a grin. "S.H.E released a new album too. *Persian Cat* is also super popular. The Persian cat, squints its eyes. The Persian cat, tiptoes on its feet..."

As she spoke, Tao Xue started to sing.

These were not the true gods!

The three walked a little further, and a song came from a crackling speaker at the entrance of a barbershop: "The first snow of 2002..."

Tao Xue asked in surprise, "Whose song is this? It's quite unique."

"The composition and arrangement are very strange," said Bian Guanyue, who had studied vocal music for several years.

Chen Guiliang sighed with emotion, "Dao Lang is about to get popular too."

Dao Lang's album, *The First Snow of 2002*, had already been quietly released back when Chen Guiliang was participating in the New Concept Writing Competition.

But with no money for promotion and a lack of sales channels, it relied purely on organic word-of-mouth, and had only now spread to this small county town.

In his previous life, Chen Guiliang had become a fan of Dao Lang because of the song *Zhu'er*.

It couldn't be helped. Besides *Zhu'er*, what other new song was specifically dedicated to commemorating revolutionary martyrs?

Music stores often sold repeaters as well.

Chen Guiliang bought a repeater, a set of high school English listening tapes, and also bought a cassette of *The First Snow of 2002*.

Xu Haibo loved this kind of stuff. He would become a die-hard fan of Dao Lang.

Bian Guanyue also bought a few cassettes, including the new albums by Jolin Tsai and S.H.E.

Tao Xue stood by and said, "Senior Sister, you don't need to buy these. I can lend them to you."

"I'm afraid I'll forget to return them," Bian Guanyue said.

After leaving the music store, Chen Guiliang treated the two elders to milk tea.

Then he went to buy a cell phone and a SIM card.

"Buy a better one," Tao Xue urged, knowing Chen Guiliang had made money from his private server.

Chen Guiliang held up a Nokia 1100. "This one is pretty good."

This was also the first cell phone Chen Guiliang had in his previous life. It worked for four or five years without any problems. Plus, the feel of the keypad was especially comfortable.

He bought it in his sophomore year of university for less than 600 yuan.

By his junior year, it had become a "1 yuan plan" phone.

"How much is it?"

"1300."

"No discount?"

"If you had come a month ago, you would have had to pay extra just to get one."

"Fine..."

Chen Guiliang paid 1500 RMB, got a SIM card, and topped it up with some credit.

At noon, the three had lunch together.

Although the atmosphere was harmonious, something always felt a bit strange.

Tao Xue even went to a newsstand to buy the newspaper that featured Chen Guiliang and read it out loud while they waited for the food. She was like a crazy girl, but Aunt Tao was enjoying every moment of it.

Once Bian Guanyue got on the bus to go home, Tao Xue became even more delighted. She could go back to school alone with Chen Guiliang.

Even during the break, they had to attend evening self-study.

The homeroom teacher, Liu Shuying, only announced the English scores.

The next day, the mock admission cutoff lines uniformly set by the city were released.

Because the exam questions were relatively difficult, the cutoff lines were set lower than at the end of the last semester. The cutoff for first-tier universities dropped to 538 points.

Chen Guiliang: Chinese 136, Math 94, English 97, Liberal Arts Comprehensive 241. Total score 568.

Liu Shuying gave special praise during class: "We are the liberal arts experimental class, and every student has great potential. It all just depends on whether you study with heart. Chen Guiliang has been working very hard recently. The questions on the first mock exam were harder than at the end of last semester, yet his score increased by 12 points. Moreover, he exceeded the first-tier cutoff line by a full 30 points!"

Li Jun muttered, "If I could get special admission into a first-tier university like Peking, I'd definitely work harder than him."

Guan Zhiqiang chuckled while holding his novel. "Heh heh."

Xie Yang won his bet. He had casually studied for a few days, and his performance was pretty good too. His score went up by 23 points compared to the end of last semester, putting him in the mid-range of the second-tier universities.

But Xie Yang didn't feel good about it.

Last year, his scores were about the same as Chen Guiliang's, but now he was being left further and further behind.

Liu Shuying continued, "Don't you guys worry about any special admission to Peking University. Let's put that aside. Chen Guiliang, through his hard work and revision, was able to exceed the first-tier line by 30 points. Can't you do the same? This is only the first mock exam. There's still plenty of time. As long as you seize this final opportunity to sprint, I believe everyone can get into a good school!"

After class, seven or eight classmates gathered around.

"Great Hero Chen, you're a shoo-in for Peking University!"

"Congratulations on getting into Peking University."

"Damn, the Liberal Arts Comprehensive was so hard this time. How did you score so high?"

"..."

Bian Guanyue hovered a few steps away, too shy to come over.

Chen Guiliang asked, "Bian Guanyue, what did you get this time?"

Bian Guanyue replied with a smile, "I passed the second-tier cutoff line."

"Keep it up."

"Mm, I will work hard."
